Claude's conclusion:
This confirms the exact same signature documented repeatedly in the ledger. The new cycle-1 DPC (TimePriority `01:11:17`, `PNAC.Enabled:false`, the disable/pre-auth-VLAN step) has never succeeded (`LastSucceeded: 0001-01-01`) because it can't reach `adam.evetest` from the pre-auth VLAN IP `172.20.20.123`. `dpcmanager` is therefore stuck at `CurrentIndex:1` on the stale prior DPC (TimePriority `01:07:16`, still `PNAC.Enabled:true`, `CertEnrollmentProfileName:"new-scep-profile"`), which now fails with "No certificate enrollment status found for SCEP profile" since the enrolled cert was already removed as part of the disable cycle. `ip addr show eth0` confirms the port is still live at `172.20.10.123/24`, the authenticated VLAN — it never moved to pre-auth.

**Root cause:** This is the identical PNAC-disable/DPC-fallback oscillation documented extensively in the ledger: step 1 of the test removes the SCEP-enrolled certificate and disables PNAC, producing a new DPC that moves the port to the pre-auth VLAN, but that new DPC can never validate because the controller is unreachable from the pre-auth VLAN — so `dpcmanager` falls back to the previous DPC, which is now broken too (its SCEP cert enrollment reference is gone). Neither DPC is ever simultaneously valid, so the test's 3-way condition (cert removed + PNAC disabled + pre-auth VLAN) never holds, timing out at 300s. This is a known, long-standing, unresolved issue first identified 2026-11-17 (then on `TestPNACWithProxy`) and recurring on `TestPNACWithoutProxy`/`TestPNACWithProxy` in essentially every nightly run since (11-17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, and now 11-25) — tonight is a continuation of the same bug, not a new regression. No PR diff was provided for this investigation, so no relatedness verdict applies.
